purpose: Tranylcypromine is used to treat depression, especially when other antidepressants have not worked. It can help improve your mood, energy, sleep, and overall sense of well-being. Doctors may also use it for certain anxiety-related conditions.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers like serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine to regulate your mood. An enzyme called monoamine oxidase breaks these chemicals down too quickly in some people with depression. Tranylcypromine blocks that enzyme, so these mood-boosting chemicals build up and stay active longer in your brain.
common_side_effects: Dizziness when standing up quickly, dry mouth, trouble sleeping or vivid dreams, headache, restlessness, rapid heartbeat, constipation, and mild swelling in the legs or feet.
warnings: This medication has very serious dietary restrictions — you MUST avoid foods high in tyramine such as aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented products, red wine, and beer, or you could have a dangerous spike in blood pressure called a hypertensive crisis. It also interacts with many medications including other antidepressants, cold medicines, and pain relievers, so always tell every doctor and pharmacist you take this drug. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor. It is not safe during pregnancy.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg taken twice a day, often in the morning and afternoon. Your doctor may slowly increase this to 30 mg per day or sometimes higher based on how you respond. It is generally taken in the morning or early afternoon to avoid sleep problems at night.
